_note: How much a lens's sampled scalar derivatives moved when the anchor they were read at was
displaced, by model and by layer. Data rather than code because it is a measurement of one
model at three of its layers, and nothing may be carried across from a neighbouring layer or
a different checkpoint. A model absent here has not been measured, and a cross-path reading
on it is refused for that reason rather than allowed for want of a figure.
Source: WS-D's float32 displacement control (e771c2b), recomputed from all 108 committed
scalar rows by WS-A's map/anchor audit (ca396fb), which is the authority for these values.
WITHDRAWN by that audit: the amplification ratios once reported at these three layers, and
they are not restated here in any form, not even to name them. They divided a derivative
change by a displacement norm taken at one position while the
intervention replaced the whole sequence, so they are not condition estimates and are not
recorded here in any form. A ratio of one scalar projection over a finite displacement is a
directional sensitivity measurement in any case, not a worst-case condition number.

google/gemma-3-4b-it.basis: WS-D float32 displacement control (e771c2b), recomputed by WS-A's audit (ca396fb)
google/gemma-3-4b-it.label: sampled displacement, one draw, eighteen projections
google/gemma-3-4b-it.quantity: absolute change of each scalar derivative relative to its own baseline
reading_notes: A median alone does not say the layer is safe: at layer 33 the float32 median is 0.125 and
the maximum over the same eighteen projections is 91.9, so 'the last block is well
conditioned' does not follow from the median (audit ca396fb).
An equal-norm random displacement moves the derivatives as much or more, so the sampled
displacement is not a special direction.
native_anchor_read_in_the_float32_tail holds the tail in float32 and switches only the
anchor. Both of its readings use the float32 tail, so it is NOT a native-against-float32
comparison and it does not measure the lens/capture crossing, which remains unmeasured.
